title: Pager playbook: runbook indexing, rotation lifecycle, and customer-notice patterns
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents Redwood's opinionated approach to pager lifecycle management, the runbook indexing schema we use, practical on-call rotation rules, a lightweight game-day exercise specifically for pager escalation paths, and a library of customer communication templates tailored to severity tiers. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, support leads, and incident commanders.

Why this exists
---------------
We observed repeated latency in incident response when: runbooks were hard to find, escalation chains were ambiguous, and customer comms were drafted ad-hoc. This page prescribes a single, searchable structure for runbooks, a predictable rotation policy that balances cognitive load, and tested notification templates for consistent external communication.

Ownership and scope
--------------------
- Document owner: Maya Patel (eng-sre)
- Operational owner: SRE rotations squad
- Applies to: all production-facing services (redwood-api, inference-runtime, routing-proxy, batch-workers)
- Exclusions: onboarding prototypes in /sandbox namespaces

Quick definitions
-----------------
- Pager: any push notification (SMS/email/slack) triggered by an alert rule and routed through PagerDuty/Opsgenie.
- Primary: the on-call engineer who must acknowledge within configured SLO.
- Secondary: the escalation contact after Primary (if unresponsive).
- Incident Commander (IC): appointed during severity>=P1 incidents.

Indexing runbooks (how to write/find a runbook)
------------------------------------------------
We maintain a runbook library in Confluence that must follow the Runbook Index Schema below. Every runbook should be titled and tagged for discovery and include a short reproducible checklist. Search relies on the following fields: service, trigger-patterns, preconditions, owner, last-tested.

Runbook Index Schema (copyable template)
| Field | Required | Example | Notes |
|-------|----------|---------|-------|
| Title | yes | redis-leader-election-fallback | short kebab-case name |
| Service | yes | routing-proxy | used for per-service dashboards |
| Triggers | yes | artifacts: 500ms p90 CPU > 85% for 10m | exact alert names used by monitoring |
| Preconditions | optional | minimal traffic, debug-logs-enabled | things to check before proceeding |
| Steps | yes | numbered checklist | each step should be < 6 bullets |
| Rollback | optional | revert conf, restart pod | short and tested |
| Last-tested | yes | 2026-01-08 | date of last game-day or incident use |
| Owner | yes | @service-oncall (Slack) | rotation team alias or person |

Example runbook header (copy into new runbook)
```
Title: routing-proxy-connection-saturation
Service: routing-proxy
Triggers: alert-routing-proxy-cxn-saturation
Preconditions: verify downstream kv-cache is healthy
Owner: @routing-proxy-oncall
Last-tested: 2026-01-18
```

Checklist style and conventions
- Use numbered steps for the canonical path (1..N).
- After the canonical path include a short section "If this does not restore:" with escalation steps.
- Include exact CLI commands and playbook-safe timeouts.
- Add a short diagnostics section with key graph panels to check.

Rotation lifecycle and fairness rules
-----------------------------------
Goals: predictable coverage, reasonable fatigue limits, and fast handoffs.

Minimum constraints (enforced by scheduler):
- Shift length: 1 week for primary rotations (Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59).
- Maximum primaries per month per engineer: 2.
- Minimum rest between shifts: 6 days.
- Backup/secondary rotation: on-call for weekends only if assigned as backup.

Succession rules (if a primary is unavailable)
1. Primary doesn't acknowledge within ack-window (default 8 minutes) -> Pager escalates to Secondary.
2. Secondary doesn't acknowledge in 10 minutes -> OpsLead on-call escalates.
3. OpsLead escalates to SRE manager if still unacknowledged after 20 minutes.

Schedule examples
- Example rotation entry (Calendar / iCal format):
```
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
SUMMARY:Routing Proxy - Primary Oncall
DTSTART:20260202T000000Z
DTEND:20260209T235900Z
DESCRIPTION:Primary oncall for routing-proxy
END:VCALENDAR
```

Automated fairness algorithm (scheduler behavior)
- The rotation scheduler (internal tool: rota-service) computes assignment with these weights: prefer engineers with fewer primaries in last 90 days (-2 penalty per prior primary), prefer volunteers (+5 score), disfavor holiday-week assignments (-3 penalty). Manual swaps allowed with approval from rotation lead and log annotation.

Acknowledgment and SLOs
-----------------------
SLOs for pager response:
- P1: Primary ack within 5 minutes (target 95%).
- P2: Primary ack within 15 minutes (target 95%).
- P3: Primary ack within 60 minutes (target 90%).
If SLO is violated, auto-create a postmortem stub and notify the rotation lead.

Game-day: pager escalation exercise (90-minute template)
-------------------------------------------------------
Objective: Verify the full pager chain, runbook discoverability, and customer communication timing. Run frequency: quarterly per service-team. Participants: primary, secondary, rotation lead, product incident champion, SRE on-call shadow.

Agenda (90 minutes):
1. 00:00–00:10 — Setup and goals (rotation lead)
2. 00:10–00:30 — Inject alert A: simulate P1 (pager trigger to primary)
3. 00:30–00:50 — Force primary unavailability to validate automatic escalation to secondary
4. 00:50–01:05 — IC appointment and runbook execution walkthrough (make changes in a safe staging mimic)
5. 01:05–01:20 — Draft customer notice and status page update (timed exercise)
6. 01:20–01:30 — Retrospective and action item capture

Success criteria:
- Alert reached primary and then secondary per timings.
- Runbook found and executed within 20 minutes.
- Status page draft produced in under 10 minutes.

Post-game deliverables:
- Mark runbooks with last-tested date.
- Create followup tasks for any automation gaps.

Pager tooling snippets
---------------------
PagerDuty integration example (minimal policy)
```json
{
  "rule": "match(alert.source == \"routing-proxy\")",
  "delay_seconds": 0,
  "escalation_sequence": ["primary","secondary","opslead"]
}
```
Slack automation (examples to run in #oncall-ops)
```bash
# Acknowledge incident from slack (bot alias: @opsbot)
/opsbot ack INC-12345 --who @me
# Escalate to manager
/opsbot escalate INC-12345 --to @opslead
```
Health checks and telemetry for runbook confidence
--------------------------------------------------
Each runbook should reference 3 core telemetry panels to validate preconditions:
- panel_1: requests/s and p95 latency (service-dashboard:latency)
- panel_2: error-rate 5m (service-dashboard:errors)
- panel_3: queue depth (kafka-instance:consumer-lag)

If any of these panels are missing the runbook must include a short note: "Missing telemetry: @metrics-team to add within 2 weeks".

Customer communication patterns
------------------------------
We use a tiered template system so customers receive consistent messages. Replace bracketed fields before publish. For all public messages confidentiality is "internal" unless security/legal approves restricted wording.

Severity mapping to external cadence
- P1 (major service outage affecting >10% customers): initial notice within 15 minutes; updates every 30 minutes until mitigation; post-incident report within 72 hours.
- P2 (partial degradation): initial notice within 1 hour; updates hourly until resolved; post-incident report within 7 business days.
- P3 (minor impact): initial notice optional; summary included in monthly incident digest.

Public status page template (short)
Title: Degraded performance for routing-proxy
Impact: Some API requests returned 5xx from 12:07 UTC affecting ~12% of requests.
Status: Identified — Mitigation in progress
Updated: 2026-02-08 12:25 UTC
Next update: 2026-02-08 12:55 UTC
Details: We have identified increased connection saturation to the routing-proxy cluster. Engineers are applying a targeted configuration and routing-rebalance.

Customer notice templates (copy/paste and edit)
P1 initial (15m):
"Redwood customers — We are investigating elevated errors impacting API requests for some customers. Our engineering team has identified the likely source and is actively mitigating. We will post an update within 30 minutes. If you rely on dedicated capacity, your account team will follow up directly. Status page: {status_url}"

P2 update (hourly):
"Update: We are continuing mitigation efforts for degraded requests. Key action in-flight: rolling rebalancing of routing-proxy instances to reduce connection saturation. Expected next update in 60 minutes. If you are experiencing critical business impact, contact support@redwood.ai with priority tag 'P2-Impact'."

After-action report cadence and minimum content
------------------------------------------------
For incidents meeting any of the following: P1, user-visible data loss, or SLA breach — a postmortem is required and must be published within 5 business days. Minimum content:
- Timeline (UTC) of events
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Contributing factors
- Remediation plan with owners and dates
- Action items tracked in Jira (links)
- Severity and customer impact summary

Automated triggers for postmortem creation
- Alert for P1 acknowledged: auto-create postmortem stub in /postmortems with owner set to IC.
- SLO breach detected via the SLO service: create postmortem stub and notify engineering leadership.

Appendices and reference material
--------------------------------
- Playbook for appointing an IC (short): IC should be a senior engineer or rotation lead; confirm communications lead and designate notetaker.
- Escalation contact table (kept up-to-date in secure vault):
| Role | Contact | When to call |
|------|---------|-------------|
| OpsLead | opslead@redwood.ai | if primary+secondary fail to ack in 30m |
| SRE Manager | sre-manager@redwood.ai | escalation after OpsLead if incident active >60m |

- Links: runbook template (confluence://templates/runbook-template), rota-service (gitlab://rota-service), pagerduty-config (vault://pagerduty/redwood-config).

How to contribute and change-control
-----------------------------------
- Small edits (<3 lines) may be done via PR to the runbook and reviewed asynchronously.
- Changes to rotation policy or SLOs require approval by SRE leadership and an entry in the decision log (ADR).
